Are macros resolved inside a Base64-encoded CommandText?
qa.answer: Yes. With the Base64 switch set, the action decodes CommandText and then resolves its macros, because the engine cannot see macros while the value is encoded. CommandFile content keeps its macros as written.

description: ### Purpose
Runs an aggregation pipeline on a MongoDB collection.
Covers the work a relational flow would give to a stored procedure or a grouped query: grouping, joining, reshaping, and writing results into another collection.
Stores the produced documents as relaxed Extended JSON, which keeps the BSON types plain JSON cannot express.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature                    | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| Pipeline as data           | Reads the stages from CommandText, CommandFile, or Base64-encoded text and binds them as BSON.                                                     |
| One or many stages         | Accepts a JSON array of stages, or a single stage object with no array wrapper.                                                                     |
| Writing pipelines          | A pipeline that ends in `$merge` or `$out` writes its result and then reports the documents of the written collection.                             |
| Large pipelines            | The AllowDiskUse switch lets a stage spill to disk when it exceeds the server memory limit.                                                          |
| Field names                | Reports the union of the top-level field names of the produced documents, in first-seen order.                                                       |
| Session and entity outputs | Stores outputs as Base64 session parameters named `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:<Name>` and returns them in the response entity unless `NoEntity` is set.  |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case             | Description                                                                               |
| Daily rollup         | Group the documents of a day into totals and write them into a summary collection.        |
| Joined extract       | Join two collections with `$lookup` and export the joined documents a bot processes.      |
| Deduplication        | Group by a business key to find and report duplicate documents.                           |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case            | Description                                                                          |
| Aggregate assertion | Compare a grouped total with the value the system under test displays.               |
| Fixture shaping     | Reshape stored fixtures into the document shape a test needs.                         |
| Data audit          | Group the documents a test wrote to confirm the expected distribution.                |
### Notes
An empty pipeline fails the step, because an aggregation without stages has nothing to run.
A pipeline that ends in `$merge` or `$out` returns no documents of its own, so the driver reads the written collection instead and the step reports those documents.
The server rejects `$merge` and `$out` inside a transaction, so a writing pipeline runs without the Transaction switch and is not rolled back.
Outputs are plain text in the response entity and Base64-encoded in the session parameters.
Stores the union of the top-level field names of the produced documents, as a JSON array.
Reports the field names in the order they were first seen, which follows the last projecting stage.
Returned as plain text in the response entity for direct data transfer.

edge_cases: Group stage exceeds the memory limit without AllowDiskUse
Pipeline passed as a single object instead of an array
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the grouped documents in `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:Result` and the stage count in `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:StageCount`.
annotations.notes: The stages bind as BSON, so their values never become part of a composed command. An empty result is reported as an empty array with a count of 0.

description: ### Group documents into totals
The argument names the collection and passes a two-stage pipeline that matches and groups.

The pipeline is Base64-encoded, because its nested stages contain `}}`, which would end the inline argument value; the decoded text is `[{"$match":{"status":"open"}},{"$group":{"_id":"$sku","total":{"$sum":"$total"}}}]`.
The step stores the grouped documents as relaxed Extended JSON.

edge_cases: Transaction switch set together with $merge, which the server rejects
annotations.expected_result: The step writes the rollup into the target collection and then reports the documents of that collection, so DocumentCount matches the number of merged documents.
annotations.notes: MongoDB rejects $merge and $out inside a transaction, so a writing pipeline runs without the Transaction switch. Use $merge with an explicit whenMatched rule when the target already holds documents.

description: ### Write a rollup into another collection
The argument passes a pipeline that groups and then merges the result into a summary collection.
The pipeline is Base64-encoded, because its nested stages contain `}}`; the decoded text is `[{"$group":{"_id":"$sku","total":{"$sum":"$total"}}},{"$merge":{"into":"sku-totals"}}]`.
The step runs without the `Transaction` switch, because MongoDB rejects `$merge` inside a transaction.
After the merge, the driver reads the written collection, so the step reports the merged documents instead of an empty result.

edge_cases: CommandFile points to a missing file
File holds an object that is not a stage
Pipeline needs more time than CommandTimeout allows
annotations.expected_result: The step reads the pipeline from the file and stores the produced documents in `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:Result`.
annotations.notes: A long pipeline belongs in a file, which also keeps it reviewable. Raise CommandTimeout and set AllowDiskUse for a heavy pipeline.

description: ### Run a pipeline from a file
The argument reads the stages from a UTF-8 file, raises the time budget, and allows disk use.
The file content is always read as plain text, so the Base64 switch never applies to it.

edge_cases: Connection URI names hosts that form no replica set, so the transaction fails
Pipeline file is missing or holds no JSON array
Credentials parameter set together with ConnectionString
annotations.expected_result: The step runs the pipeline of the file inside a transaction and stores its documents in `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:Documents`.
annotations.notes: ConnectionString applies only when Credentials is not set. A transaction needs a replica set or a sharded cluster, which the replicaSet option of the URI names. The pipeline comes from a file because an inline pipeline ends in two closing braces.

description: ### Aggregate with a replica-set connection URI
The argument passes a complete MongoDB connection URI that names both replica-set members and the set itself, which a transaction requires.
The pipeline is read from a UTF-8 file, so its nested stage documents never pass through the inline argument value.

edge_cases: Base64 switch is absent, so the macro inside the encoded text stays hidden and is not resolved
Value is passed plain, so the engine resolves its macros before the plugin runs
The payload comes from CommandFile, so its macros are kept as written
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the per-SKU totals of the orders created today in `InvokeMongoDbAggregate:Result`.
annotations.notes: The engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs, when the Base64 value still hides them, so the plugin resolves the macros of the decoded payload itself. Encoding also keeps the closing braces of the JSON from ending the inline argument value.

description: ### Total today's orders with a Base64 pipeline that holds a macro
The argument binds the `mongo-production` credentials, a Base64 CommandText, and the Base64 switch at runtime.

The decoded payload is `[{"$match":{"createdOn":{"$gte":"{{$New-Date --Format:yyyy-MM-dd}}"}}},{"$group":{"_id":"$sku","total":{"$sum":"$total"}}}]`; the New-Date macro is resolved after decoding, so the server receives the current date.
Stores the union of the top-level field names of the produced documents, as a JSON array.
Reports the field names in the order they were first seen, which follows the last projecting stage.
The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before comparing or displaying it.

description: Lets a pipeline stage write temporary files when it exceeds the server memory limit.
Set it for a large group or sort stage, which otherwise fails with a memory-limit error.
parameters.name: AllowDiskUse

description: Reads CommandText as UTF-8 Base64 and decodes it before use.
After decoding, the macros in the decoded value are resolved, because the engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs and cannot see them while the value is encoded.
Use it for a payload that contains ` --` or `}}`, which end an inline argument value.
Invalid Base64 fails the step, so an encoded payload never reaches the server as text.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Names the collection the step operates on, such as `orders` or `shop.orders`.
A name qualified as `database.collection` selects its own database and overrides the Database parameter.
The name is split on its first dot only, so `shop.price.history` addresses the collection `price.history`.
parameters.name: Collection

description: Reads the payload from a UTF-8 file, such as `C:\flows\filter.json`.
Applies only when CommandText is not set, so an inline payload always takes priority.
The Base64 switch never applies here; file content is always read as plain text.
parameters.name: CommandFile

description: Supplies the pipeline as a JSON array of stage objects, such as `[{"$match":{"status":"open"}},{"$count":"open"}]`.
A single stage object is accepted too, so a one-stage pipeline needs no array wrapper.
Required, because an aggregation without stages has nothing to run.
parameters.name: CommandText

description: Sets the time budget, in seconds, for connecting, selecting a server, and running the operation.
The value 0 means no operation timeout, so the step waits until the server answers.
Raise it for a long aggregation and lower it for a health check that must fail fast.
parameters.name: CommandTimeout

description: Supplies a full MongoDB connection URI, such as `mongodb://localhost:27017/shop`.
Applies only when Credentials is not set, so a stored credentials reference always takes priority.
Every connection setting, such as the host, the login, the replica set, and the TLS mode, is written into the URI itself.
parameters.name: ConnectionString

description: Names a stored MongoDB credentials record by name or id, such as `mongo-production`, so secrets stay out of the rule.
The record carries the host, port, login, replica set, and TLS settings, so the step never repeats them.
A value that carries a URI scheme, such as `mongodb://`, is used as a raw connection URI instead, and any other value that matches no record fails the step.
parameters.name: Credentials

description: Names the database the step operates on, such as `shop`.
Selects the database next to the collection, and replaces the database the credentials record or the connection URI carries.
A collection named as `database.collection` overrides this parameter in turn.
parameters.name: Database

description: Omits the response entity, so the step reports its outputs only as session parameters.
Use it when a later step reads the outputs by name and no data transfer is needed.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Runs the pipeline inside a multi-document transaction, so it reads one consistent snapshot.
MongoDB rejects the `$merge` and `$out` stages inside a transaction, so a writing pipeline runs without this switch.
MongoDB supports transactions only on a replica set or a sharded cluster; a standalone server fails the step.
parameters.name: Transaction
